newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds toppy for now, but 101.36 to hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds toppy for now, but 101.36 to hold.

text.p: LIFFE September Bund futures will need to digest their latest gains before they can re-challenge the June peak of 101.88, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
Anne Whitby, head of technical analysis at 4CAST, said a heavy congestion area from Tuesday's high of 101.73 would weigh on the market. But it would hold above 101.36 support.
"Probably what we're looking for in the short term is ranging and then another challenge at 101.73," Whitby said.
"Short term we're going to do some consolidation before we can push into that."
By 0700 GMT, September Bunds were 0.08 lower at 101.56.
Bunds rallied after a low of 101.10 on Tuesday, finishing at a technically encouraging 101.64.

Whitby pegged support at 101.52, which is a congestion area below the market and close to the session low, followed by Monday's high of 101.46. Key support was 101.36, which is where the last surge started from, she said.
"I shouldn't think that we'd come back and test as low as that. If that did break it would be quite serious," Whitby said.
Although upside prospects were bright, the market would have trouble just now at conquering the June 17 high of 101.88. After that level, there was further strong resistance at 101.99.
Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London said Wednesday's weak start should be considered as profit taking after a good rally, with charts looking constructive.
"While 101.37 holds intact, impulse structure to the upside remains valid," he said.
Diebel saw gains to 101.88, and possibly extending to the 102.05 target.
However in the unlikely event of breaching 101.37, Bunds would be exposed to the 101.05/08 area, he said.
September Euromark futures stood 0.01 higher at 96.84.
